:::{#thm-indpt-uncorrelated}
#### Independent random variables have zero covariance

If $X$ and $Y$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt),
each [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) or [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv),
with defined [expectations](expectation.qmd#def-expectation),
then:

$$\E{XY} = \E{X}\E{Y}$$

If also $\E{X^2} < \infty$ and $\E{Y^2} < \infty$, then $\Cov{X,Y} = 0$.

:::

::: proof

Write $f_X$ and $f_Y$ for the PMFs or densities of $X$ and $Y$,
with reference measures $\measure_X$ and $\measure_Y$ as in
the [joint-distribution form of Fubini--Tonelli](expectation.qmd#cor-fubini-joint)
([counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#def-counting-measure) for a [discrete variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv),
[Lebesgue measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#def-lebesgue-measure) for a [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) one).
Because $X$ and $Y$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt),
$f_{X,Y}(x, y) = f_X(x)\,f_Y(y)$ is their [joint PMF](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-pmf), [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf), or density-mass [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function)
(the factorization in the notes to the [definition of independence](independence.qmd#def-indpt)).
First, with $h(x, y) = \abs{x}\abs{y} \ge 0$ (condition (a)):

$$
\ba
\E{\abs{XY}}
&= \int_{\rangef{X}}\paren{\int_{\rangef{Y}} \abs{x}\abs{y}\,f_X(x)\,f_Y(y)\,d\measure_Y(y)}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(joint-distribution form of Fubini--Tonelli, condition (a))} \\
&= \int_{\rangef{X}} \abs{x}\,f_X(x)\paren{\int_{\rangef{Y}} \abs{y}\,f_Y(y)\,d\measure_Y(y)}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(} \abs{x}\,f_X(x) \text{ does not depend on } y \text{)} \\
&= \int_{\rangef{X}} \abs{x}\,f_X(x) \cd \E{\abs{Y}}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(LOTUS for } \abs{Y} \text{)} \\
&= \E{\abs{X}} \cd \E{\abs{Y}}
&& \text{(LOTUS for } \abs{X} \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is finite, because $X$ and $Y$ have defined [expectations](expectation.qmd#def-expectation). <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
So condition (b) holds,
and the same steps without the [absolute values](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-absolute-value) give: <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$
\ba
\E{XY}
&= \int_{\rangef{X}}\paren{\int_{\rangef{Y}} xy\,f_X(x)\,f_Y(y)\,d\measure_Y(y)}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(joint-distribution form of Fubini--Tonelli, condition (b))} \\
&= \int_{\rangef{X}} x\,f_X(x)\paren{\int_{\rangef{Y}} y\,f_Y(y)\,d\measure_Y(y)}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(} x\,f_X(x) \text{ does not depend on } y \text{)} \\
&= \int_{\rangef{X}} x\,f_X(x) \cd \E{Y}\,d\measure_X(x)
&& \text{(definition of expectation)} \\
&= \E{X} \cd \E{Y}
&& \text{(definition of expectation)}
\ea
$$

Finally, by the [alternative formula for covariance](#thm-alt-cov):

$$
\ba
\Cov{X,Y}
&= \E{XY} - \E{X}\E{Y}
&& \text{(alternative formula for covariance)} \\
&= \E{X}\E{Y} - \E{X}\E{Y}
&& \text{(} \E{XY} = \E{X}\E{Y} \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

:::
